Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council, PCD 21

FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized Ly me Plastics Containers Sectional Committee had been approved by the-Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. Vunusputi are presently packed in tin containers, laminated paper boards, blow-moulded HDPE containers and flexible pouches/packs. Indian Standards havealready been formulatedonthese subjects_[lS 10325 : 1989 Square tins - 15 kg for ghee, vanuspati, edible oils and bakery shortenings - Specification ( first revision )`, IS 10339 : 1988 `Specification for ghee, vunusputi and edible oils tins (first revision )`, IS 143 19 : 1995 `Laminated paper board pack for vunusputi - Specification', IS 10840 : 1994 `Blow mouldedHDPE containers for packing of vunusputi- Specification ( secondrevision )`, IS 11352 : 1998 `Flexible pouches for the packing of vunusputi up to 5 kg or 5 litres - Specification ( second revision )' and 1s 14 129 : 1994 `Flexible packaging material for packing of vunusputi in 10 kg and 15 kg packs - Specification' 1. With the increase in usage of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) containers also for-packaging of vunuspati, the Sectional Committee decided to prepare a separate standard on this subject. Jn accordance with the Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodities) Third Amendment Rules, 1994, that edible oils, ghee, vunusputi and butter oils may bepacked by weight or volume basis in sizes of 50 g, 100 g, 200 g, 500 g, 1 kg, 2 kg, 5 kg or 50 ml, 100 ml, 200 ml, 500 ml,1 litre, 2 litres, 5 litres thereafter in multiples of 5 kg or 5 litres.The rule also states that in case packing has been done on mass basis declaration of volume within brackets, and if it is done on volume basis declaration of mass within brackets is to be done. Keeping this in view, provisions have been made in this standard to permit to pack vunusputi on volume basis also. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. 7'he number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 14764 : ~2000

Indian Standard
POLYETHYLENE TEREPHTHALATE ( PET ) CONTAINERS FOR PACKAGING OF VANASPATISPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE IS No.

Title Polypropylene and propylene copolymers thermoplastics Designation Polyalkylene terephthalate (PET a PBT ) for its safe use in contact with foodstuffs, pharmaceuticals and drinking water Polyalkylene terephthalate ( PET & PBT ) for moulding and extrusion

This standard covers the requirements, methods of sampling and tests for stretch blow moulded polyethylene terephthalate (PET) containers for packaging of vanaspati in quantities of I kg, 2 kg and 5 kg or 1 litre, 2 litres and 5 litres. 2 NOBMA'llW . REFERENCES

4.1 Material 4.1.1 Container Do& The material used for the container body shall be polyethylene terephthalate (PET) conforming to, IS 13193. 4.1.1.1 The material shall be of food grade polyethylene terephthalate (PET) conforming to IS 12252. 4.1.1.2 The pigments and colourants used shall be as per the lists prescribed in IS 9833. 4.1.2 Handle and Closure The material used for the handles and closures shall be of HDPE generally of grade designation PE MAN A57 T200 conforming to IS 7328 or of polypropylene generally of grade designation PP-HM-95-030-Nat or PP-HC-95-030-Nat conforming to IS 1095 1. 4.1.2.1 The material shall also be of food grade HDPE conforming to IS 10146 or of food grade polypropylene conforming to IS 109~10. 4.1.2.2 The pigments and colourants used shall be as per the lists prescribed in IS 9833. 4.1.2.3 Steel/MS rods or any other suitable materials, duly protected with polish or paints to avoid rust, may also be used provided it does not come in contact with the product (vanaspati); thickness of the rod be agreed between the purchaser and the supplier.

4.2 Manufacture 4.2.1 The container shall be manufactured by stretch blow moulding; the handle and the top closure shall be made by injection moulding. 1 kg or 1 litre and 2 kg or 2 litres containers may or may not be provided with the handle but 5 kg or 5 Iitres containers shall be provided with a handle. 4.2.2 The container, closure and the handle shall be free from any visual defects like local thinning, warping, burning and non-uniform colour dispersion. 4.3 Capacity The minimum brimful capacity of the container when checked in accordance with the method given in 5 of IS 2798 shall be as under: Container Capacity +I$ 1 2 5 Container Capacity (litres) I 2 5 Minimum Brimful Capacity (kg) 1160 2300 5700 Minimum Brimful Capacity (ml) 1040 2070 5 130

4.6 Wall Thickness The wall thickness shall be measured in accordance with the method given in 4.5 of IS 2798. The minimum wall thickness at any point of the container shall be not less than 0.20 mm for containers of I and 2 kg or 1 and 2 litres capacity, 0.30 mm-for the containers of 5 kg or 5 litres.
NOTE The wall thickness of the container is subject over the total area. to variation

4.7 Tests 4.7.1 Closure Leakage Test The containers filled with water at ambient temperature and closed tight with the closure with inner seal heatsealed to its mouth, shall not~show any leakages when held vertically upside down for 10 min. The container may be kept on a blotting paper in upside down position and any leakages observed shall be noted. 4.7.2 Drop Impact Test The container filled with water at standard temperature of 27 f 1�C and closed tight with the closure with inner seal heat-sealed to its mouth shall not show any sign of rupture or leakage on the part of container kody, closure, handles and the inner seal, when tested in accordancewith the method described in 8 of IS 2798. 4.7.3 Stack Load Test The containers shall not show any deformation likely to reduce their strength, cause leakage or reduction in effectiveness of the closure or cause instability in stacks when tested in accordance with the method prescribed in 9 of IS 2798. 4.7.4 Handle Pull Test The container provided with the handle when tested according to the method prescribed in 1 I of IS 2798 shall not-show any damage to the handle or the hinges. ~4.7.5 Ink Adhesion for Printed Containers The printed containers when tested in accordance with the method prescribed in 13 of IS 2798 shall not show any signiftcant removal of the print from the container surface and the print shall be legible to the naked eye after the test. 4.7.6 Product Resistance of Printed Containers The printed containers when tested in accordance with the method prescribed in 14 of IS 2798 shall not show any significant removal of the print from the container surface and the print shall be legible to the naked eye after the test. 2

NOTE - The brimful capacity of the container may be calculated on the basis of the specific gravity of vutnzsputi and may vary with the filling process and filling temperature. The purchaser ofthe container shall specify the minimum brimful capacity according to the method and temperature of his tilling.

4.4 Mass 4.4.1 The mass of the container shall be as agreed to between the~purchaser and the supplier. The mass of the lid and handle, when provided, shall not be included in the mass of the containers. The tolerance on the nominal mass of the container specified by the purchaser shall be as under: Container Capacity (kg or litre)

4.4.2 Tolerance on the nominal specified mass of the lid and the handle checked individually shall be *5 percent. 4.5 Shape and Dimension The shape and dimensions of the container shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier.

IS 14764 : 2000 47.7 Migration Test Representative samples of container shall be subjtited to overall migration test w~ithn-heptane at 27 f 2�C for 30 min either by filling the whole container or by using sheets cut from the container; in the latter case the migration value has to be extrapolated to the container contact surface area and the volume of the contents. The maximum extraction values for the container material shall not exceed 60 mg/l and 10 mg/dm* ( for details of the test, see IS 9845 ). 5 MARKING 5.1 Each container shall be permanently marked with the following: a) Indication of the source of manufacture and trade-mark, if any; b) Net quantity packed in litres ( kg ) or kg ( litres); c) Batch No. or Code No. or otherwise td enable the lot of consignment or manufacture to be traced back from records;

d Made from `food grade' plastics materials.
5.2 BIS Certification Marking The containers may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and ReguLaations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 6 SAMPLING Sampling of container shall be drawn and the criteria for conformity determined asdescribed in Annex A.

ANNEX A
( Clause 6 ) !sAMPLlNc
A-l SCALE OF SAMPLING A.l.l Lot conditions (4.2.2). Any containers failing in one or more ofthe requirements shall be termed as defective. The lot shall be acceptedunder this head, if the number of defective containers in sample does not exceed the acceptaricenumber given in co13 of Table 1. A-2.2 Brimful Capacity, Container Mass and Mass of Handle and Lid For the purpose of above tests, five containers for lot size up to 5 000 and IO containers for lot size above 5 000 shall be selected at random from the samples already drawn according to A-l .3. Each of the sample containers shall be subjected to tests for brimful capacity (4.3), container mass (4.4.1), and the mass of lid and handle (4.4.2). There shall be no failure if the lot is to be accepted under this clause. A-2.3 Test for Closure Leakage The number of sample containers to be drawn shall be in accordance with co14 of Table I. Each of tlie
sample -containers shall be subjected to closure leakage test. The number of failures shall not exceed the acceptance number given in co1 5 of Table 1. 3

In any consignment all the containers of the same material, nominal capacity and drawn from a single batch of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.

A-t.2 Scale of Sampling For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of this standard, tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. The number of containers to be sampled from a lot shall be in accordance with Table I. A-l.3 The containers shall be selected at random from the lot. To ensure the randomness of selection, methods given in 4905 may be followed. A;2 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY A-2.1 Visual Examiamation The sample containers selected as per col 2 of Table 1 shall be examined for manufacturing

IS 14764 : 2000 A-2.4 Wall ~Thickness, Ink Adhesion, Product Resistance and Migration The sub-sample size asgiven~in co16 of Table 1 shall Abesubjected to tests for wall thickness, handle pull test ink adhesion, product resistance and migration tests. No failures shall occur for acceptance of the lot under this clause. A-2.5 Drop Impact Test, Stack Load Test and Handle Pull Test One setof sample container as given in the test methods ( 4.7.2,4.7.3 and 4.7.4 ) shall be drawn from the lot and these shall be subjected to the respective tests. The sample shall pass the tests for acceptance of the lot in respect of drop impact and stacking requirements.
